content.text: Go Blue with Northwell With colorectal cancer, early detection and treatment matter. Complete our online health risk assessment—so you can take steps to safeguard your health. Complete the screening assessment What is Go Blue? Our Go Blue initiative raises awareness about the importance of colorectal cancer screening beginning at age 45 for average-risk adults. Colonoscopy remains the gold standard—as it’s the only test that both detects cancer early and helps prevent it by removing precancerous polyps. Go Blue is supported by the Northwell Cancer Institute and Katz Institute for Women’s Health. Learn more Recently diagnosed? If you or a loved one have been diagnosed with or have concerns about a gastrointestinal cancer, our nurse navigators are here to guide you through your treatment and recovery. Our nurse navigators work hand in hand with an entire team of gastrointestinal cancer specialists, including colorectal surgeons, medical oncologists, radiation oncologists and other specialists to ensure you receive the best care possible in a timely manner. They can help you with expediting appointments, coordinating your care, obtaining records and connecting you with any needed resources. Just call 833-223-4732 or email GINavigation@northwell.edu. What women need to know The five-year survival rate for colorectal cancer is over 90% if caught early, so getting a colonoscopy on time is key. Prep is easier than ever, and the procedure itself feels like “nothing.” As one patient put it, “It’s the best 30-minute nap ever!" Eileen’s story Cancer screenings save lives. In Eileen's case, she made excuses not to have her colonoscopy done—like most of us do. After a scare at 68 years young, the colonoscopy was a lifesaver.
